summary: Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She served at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015), and is attested as a visiting researcher at Minobusan University (2026).
Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and later held a post there.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist and historian. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and earned his PhD under Ernst Kuhn at Munich. He served as professor at the University of Munich (1901–1933) and directed the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907–1933).

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and Sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Lector in Italian at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University (1955–1984).

Lucien Bernot was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at INALCO and EPHE, worked as a CNRS researcher (1947–1964), served as chargé de conférences at EPHE (1961–1978), and was a professor at the Collège de France (1979–1985).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He founded the Institut d'ethnologie and held a post at the University of Paris (~1899–1927).

Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and attended the University of Paris, Leipzig, and ENLOV. He held academic posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1920–1924), University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).

Lucjan Malinowski was a linguist who studied at Uniwersytet Petersburski, Humboldt University of Berlin, University of Jena, and Jagiellonian University. He served as professor of Slavic philology at Jagiellonian University (~1877–1898).
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Ghent under Adriaan Scharpé and completed postdoctoral work at SOAS. He was a professor at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and later served as professor and Chair at the University of Pennsylvania.

Ludvig Frands Adalbert Wimmer was a linguist who earned his MA and PhD at the University of Copenhagen, studying under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He spent his career at Copenhagen, ultimately serving as Professor of Nordic Philology (1886–1910).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Hamburg under Walther Schubring and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at Allahabad, Münster, and Berlin before holding the indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1950–1978).

Ludwig Bachhofer was a historian, Indologist, and Sinologist. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Lucian Scherman, served there as Privatdozent (1927–1935), and later was Assistant Professor of Art at the University of Chicago (1935–1965).

Ludwig Diestel was a religious studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the University of Bonn (~1858–1862), University of Greifswald (~1862–1867), University of Jena (~1867–1872), and University of Tübingen (~1872–1879).

Ludwig Fritze was an Indologist who studied at Lehrerseminar Oranienburg. He worked as a teacher at teacher-training seminaries in Oranienburg (1861–1871), Zabern (1871–1873), and Drossen (1873–1885), and as Oberlehrer at Köpenick (1885–1906).

Ludwig Heinrich Kapff was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen. He served as Privatdozent at Tübingen, Rector at Karlsgymnasium Heilbronn (1843), and Ephorus at the Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren (1854–1869).

Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Dr. phil. at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin and served as professor at the University of Greifswald (1904–1945).

Ludwig Lange was a linguist and historian who studied at Göttingen under Karl Friedrich Hermann and Theodor Benfey. He held professorships in classical philology at Charles University (1853–1859), University of Giessen (1859–1871), and University of Leipzig (from 1871).

Ludwig Oster was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Richard Pischel and earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Christian Bartholomae and Salomon Lefmann.

Ludwig Poley was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Berlin and under Eugène Burnouf and Silvestre de Sacy. He held teaching posts at the University of Padua (1866) and the University of Vienna (1867).
